acceptance_criteria: cargo check -p jmap-mail-server --features sieve passes; cargo build -p jmap-mail-server (no features) passes; register_sieve_handlers is callable by consumers
design:
jmap-mail-types/Cargo.toml: add [features] sieve = []

jmap-mail-server/Cargo.toml: add [features] sieve = [jmap-mail-types/sieve]

jmap-mail-server/src/lib.rs additions (behind cfg(feature=sieve)):
- pub mod sieve;
- pub const JMAP_SIEVE_URI: &str = urtietf:params:jmap:sieve;
- pub use sieve::{SieveBackend, handle_sieve_get, handle_sieve_query, handle_sieve_set, handle_sieve_validate};
- pub fn register_sieve_handlers<B, C>(dispatcher: &mut Dispatcher<C>, backend: Arc<B>) where B: MailBackend + SieveBackend + 'static, C: Clone + Send + 'static

The register function adds 4 method names:
  SieveScript/get, SieveScript/set, SieveScript/query, SieveScript/validate

Note: no /changes or /queryChanges — draft does not define them.

Capability constant re-export: consumers need JMAP_SIEVE_URI to advertise the capability in their Session object.

Addendum: update crate-level doc comment in lib.rs to mention the sieve feature and the 4 method names it adds.
title: sieve: feature flag wiring + register_sieve_handlers
